title: Refinement and open comparison of normalized etale tensor families
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $e:U\to X$ be a separated etale finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes, where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Use ordinary unbounded small-etale constant-$A$ module derived categories, exact pullback and derived tensor [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-kun-derived-tensor]. For each chosen compactification $c$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], put $F_e^c=Re_!^c\dashv G_e^c$ with counit $\varepsilon^c$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], $S_e=D(e_{\Sigma!})\dashv e^*$ with evaluation counit [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], and let $d_e^c:F_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}S_e$ be the canonical proper-support/sum comparison [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact]. Define $\rho_e^c=((d_e^c)^{-1})^c:G_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}e^*$ by adjunction conjugacy [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], $W_e^c=G_e^cA_X$ and $\eta_e^c=u_e\circ\rho_{e,A_X}^c$, where $u$ and all pullback-composition comparisons are those of [def-pur-etale-exact-pullback-unit-composition-comparisons]. Use the specified projections $P_e^c$ of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2).

(1) If $t:F_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_e^{c'}$ is the canonical proper-refinement comparison, or a comparison through a common refinement [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], put $r=(t^{-1})^c:G_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}G_e^{c'}$. Then
$$d_e^{c'}t=d_e^c,\qquad\rho_e^{c'}r=\rho_e^c,\qquad\eta_e^{c'}r_{A_X}=\eta_e^c,$$
$$t_{M\otimes e^*K}P_{e,M,K}^c=P_{e,M,K}^{c'}(t_M\otimes1_K).$$
The comparisons satisfy identity and composition laws, so comparison through a common refinement is independent of the refinement.

(2) Let $g:X'\hookrightarrow X$ be open, let $U'=U\times_XX'$ have projections $h:U'\hookrightarrow U$ and $e':U'\to X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion], and choose a compactification $c'$ of $e'$ (in particular the pulled-back one). Write $\beta_K:h^*e^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}e'^*g^*K$ for canonical pullback composition. Let $\chi:h^*G_e^c\to G_{e'}^{c'}g^*$ be the adjunction conjugate of the canonical compact-support composition comparison
$$D(g_{\Sigma!})F_{e'}^{c'}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_e^cD(h_{\Sigma!})$$
for $ge'=eh$, with the open compact supports identified with sum extension by their $d$ comparisons, and with the composite adjunctions whose right adjoints are $G_{e'}^{c'}g^*$ and $h^*G_e^c$. Then $\chi$ is a natural isomorphism and, for every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\chi_K=(\rho_{e',g^*K}^{c'})^{-1}\circ\beta_K\circ h^*\rho_{e,K}^c.$$
Put $\xi=G_{e'}^{c'}(u_g)\circ\chi_{A_X}:h^*W_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{e'}^{c'}$. With the coefficient-unit comparisons inserted,
$$\eta_{e'}^{c'}\circ\xi=u_h\circ h^*\eta_e^c.$$
Under the canonical sum-extension open base-change comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], restriction of the sum counit is the sum counit for $e'$, and restriction of the lift-generator projection is the corresponding projection for $e'$. Restriction of $d_e^c$ is $d_{e'}^{c'}$ under the specified compact-support exchange; restriction of $P_e^c$ is $P_{e'}^{c'}$ under that exchange and the tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These statements concern the specified natural transformations, agree with (1), and are compatible with further open restrictions.

(3) Suppose natural families $v_{e,K}^c:e^*K\otimes W_e^c\to G_e^cK$ are given for these compactifications and for $e'$, and each satisfies
$$\rho_{e,K}^c\circ v_{e,K}^c=\operatorname{unitor}_{e^*K}\circ(1\otimes\eta_e^c).$$
Then
$$r_K\circ v_{e,K}^c=v_{e,K}^{c'}\circ(1\otimes r_{A_X}),$$
$$\chi_K\circ h^*v_{e,K}^c=v_{e',g^*K}^{c'}\circ(\beta_K\otimes\xi),$$
where the latter equality identifies $h^*(e^*K\otimes W_e^c)$ with $h^*e^*K\otimes h^*W_e^c$ by canonical tensor pullback. No definition of $v$ by a projection transpose, and no purity theorem, is assumed.

proof.text: Write composition from right to left. Compactification independence of the proper-support comparison gives $d^{c'}t=d^c$, including common-refinement comparisons. Hence $(d^{c'})^{-1}=t(d^c)^{-1}$. Conjugacy reverses composition, so $\rho^{c'}r=((d^{c'})^{-1})^c(t^{-1})^c=(t^{-1}(d^{c'})^{-1})^c=((d^c)^{-1})^c=\rho^c$. Evaluate at $A_X$ and postcompose with $u_e$ to obtain the equation for $\eta$. Identity and composition laws for $t$ are supplied by the compact-support comparisons; conjugacy gives the same laws for $r$. In fact $t=(d^{c'})^{-1}d^c$ and $r=(\rho^{c'})^{-1}\rho^c$, so both comparisons are independent of the common refinement.

proof.text:
Put $N=M\otimes e^*K$. The specified projection compatibility says $d^c_NP^c=p^\Sigma(d^c_M\otimes1)$, and likewise for $c'$. Therefore
$$d^{c'}_Nt_NP^c=d^c_NP^c=p^\Sigma(d^c_M\otimes1)=p^\Sigma(d^{c'}_Mt_M\otimes1)=d^{c'}_NP^{c'}(t_M\otimes1).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $d^{c'}_N$. This is the projection equation of (1), with the actual specified $P$; no alternative projection is chosen.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text:
For composable separated etale maps $a,b$, let $\sigma_{b,a}:S_bS_a\to S_{ba}$ be the nested-summand composition. Its unit under $S_bS_a\dashv a^*b^*$ inserts successively the two identity lifts: the composite-adjunction unit is $a^*(\mathrm{unit}_b)\circ\mathrm{unit}_a$. The nested-support unit identity says that flattening by $\sigma_{b,a}$ changes these two inclusions to the single inclusion for $ba$, with the canonical composite-test-object identification. Thus the conjugate of $\sigma_{b,a}$ is the canonical map $(ba)^*\to a^*b^*$: the hom bijection sends an identity to its unit, and the units just computed agree. This calculation holds on sheaves and passes termwise, with the specified compositors, to the entire derived categories. Consequently for $ge'=eh$ the conjugate of
$$a=(\sigma_{e,h})^{-1}\sigma_{g,e'}:S_gS_{e'}\longrightarrow S_eS_h$$
is exactly $\beta:h^*e^*\to e'^*g^*$. This proves the identification of this particular mate by its units, rather than identifying arbitrary isomorphisms with the same endpoints.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text:
Let $\alpha:S_gF_{e'}^{c'}\to F_e^cS_h$ be the compact-support comparison in (2). The composition normalization of the proper-support comparison, applied to $g,e'$ and $e,h$, identifies it by
$$(d_e^cS_h)\alpha=a(S_gd_{e'}^{c'}).$$
Indeed both compositions to $S_{ge'}=S_{eh}$ are the same compact-support composition comparison followed by its proper-support comparison; the specified identity and refinement laws allow all the chosen compactifications. Taking conjugates for the composite adjunctions and using pasting/change-of-adjunction compatibility gives
$$(\rho_{e'}^{c'}g^*)\chi=\beta(h^*\rho_e^c).$$
Here the open factors have already been changed to $S_g\dashv g^*$ and $S_h\dashv h^*$ as required in the statement. The preceding step identifies the remaining sum mate with $\beta$. Cancel $\rho_{e'}^{c'}$ to get the displayed formula for $\chi$. Every factor in that formula is invertible, so $\chi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text:
The coefficient-unit and composition maps specified in the statement are the canonical exact-pullback maps. Their unit coherence for $ge'=eh$ reads
$$u_{e'}e'^*(u_g)\beta_{A_X}=u_hh^*(u_e).$$
This is the unit composition equation for the two factorizations of the same map, using their canonical pullback-composition comparisons. Naturality of $\rho_{e'}$ at $u_g:g^*A_X\to A_{X'}$ and the previous step give
$$\eta_{e'}\xi=u_{e'}\rho_{e',A_{X'}}G_{e'}(u_g)\chi_{A_X}=u_{e'}e'^*(u_g)\beta_{A_X}h^*(\rho_{e,A_X})=u_hh^*(\eta_e).$$
All unit identifications here are those fixed in the question. In particular the exact/left-derived comparison used to define $u$ does not replace a canonical unit by an arbitrary one.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text: The sum counit restriction equation is precisely the derived evaluation identity of the sum-exchange/counit lemma with $w=g,w'=h$. For the projection, take sheaves $M,K$ and an etale test object $W\to X'$. A lift $s:W\to U'$ is the same lift into $U$ together with its given map to $X'$. Under the specified sum base change, both restriction/projection routes send $(s,m)\otimes k$ to $(s,m\otimes s^*k)$. These formulas are the sheaf projection maps and agree with restrictions and balancing, so induce equal sheaf maps. For unbounded derived inputs use flat-term K-flat representatives. Sum extension preserves their flatness and K-flatness, and pullback preserves such representatives. In each bidegree the totalized sum projection is exactly the displayed generator map; restriction preserves that bidegree and introduces no interchange of factors, hence no sign. The equality of the resulting chain maps descends to the derived bifunctors by K-flat localization. This establishes restriction of the specified projection for all unbounded inputs, without a constructibility or Tor-amplitude assumption.

proof.text: For the pulled-back compactification the exchange square for $d$ is exactly (1) of support-map compatibility. For an arbitrary $c'$ compose this exchange with the canonical refinement comparison; Step 1 and the refinement compatibility of the exchange make its $d$ square the same square. To check restriction of $P^c$, postcompose both candidate restriction maps with $d_{e'}^{c'}$ at the target. The exchange square for $d$ and the normalization $dP=p^\Sigma(d\otimes1)$ rewrite the first route as the restricted sum projection. The second route becomes $p^\Sigma_{e'}$ with the same source comparison. Step 6 identifies them, using the specified tensor-pullback comparison, and cancellation of $d_{e'}^{c'}$ gives equality of the two actual projection transformations. Thus neither assertion follows merely from invertibility of its endpoints.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text:
Denote the right unitor by $R$. Apply $\rho^{c'}_K$ to both proposed refinement transports of $v$. For the first one the result is
$$\rho^{c'}_Kr_Kv^c_K=\rho^c_Kv^c_K=R_{e^*K}(1\otimes\eta^c).$$
For the second it is
$$\rho^{c'}_Kv^{c'}_K(1\otimes r_{A_X})=R_{e^*K}(1\otimes\eta^{c'})(1\otimes r_{A_X})=R_{e^*K}(1\otimes\eta^c).$$
The second equalities use only the assumed normalization of each $v$, and the last equality uses Step 1. Cancel $\rho^{c'}_K$. No construction or transposition property of $v$ is involved.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text:
For open restriction apply $\rho_{e',g^*K}$ to the two maps in (3). By Step 4 the first becomes $\beta_K h^*(\rho_{e,K}v_{e,K})$. By the assumed normalization and the pullback/right-unitor identity, this is
$$R_{e'^*g^*K}\bigl(\beta_K\otimes(u_hh^*\eta_e)\bigr).$$
Here naturality of $R$ moves $\beta_K$ past the unitor, and all tensors use the fixed pullback comparison. The second route becomes
$$R_{e'^*g^*K}\bigl(\beta_K\otimes(\eta_{e'}\xi)\bigr),$$
which is equal by Step 5. Cancel $\rho_{e',g^*K}$. The unit and unitor compatibilities used here are part of canonical derived pullback monoidality, not a purity or projection-transpose theorem.

source.place: Step 1; agent expansion of canonical etale normalization and open locality

proof.text: For another open restriction, the formula of Step 4 has one intermediate factor $\rho_{e'}$ and its inverse; in the composite they cancel by naturality. The remaining pullback-composition maps compose to the single $\beta$ by the associativity equation for canonical pullback composition. The coefficient-unit composition equation gives the same statement for $\xi$. Step 1 gives the identical cancellation when a compactification comparison is inserted before or after restriction. The exchange maps for $d$ already obey these pasting and refinement laws; expressing $P$ by $d^{-1}p^\Sigma(d\otimes1)$ therefore gives the same laws for $P$. The sum counit and generator projection obey them as well: successive restrictions are restriction to the composite test object, and preserve the same lift and tensor value from Step 6. Finally each transport of $v$ becomes the same normalized map after postcomposing with the final $\rho$, by Steps 8 and 9, so cancellation proves all successive restrictions and refinement comparisons agree. This proves the remaining coherence assertions for the specified transformations.
